passage:
"Just say it, Indu," Payal whispered at the lunch benches. "Say Rani smells funny."
"But she doesn't."
"Then you can sit somewhere else."
Indu's hands went cold. She laughed a small laugh that she did not mean, and Rani looked at her food.
"That was not funny," Indu said later, at the tap. "I'm sorry, Rani."
"Why did you do it?"
"I was scared they'd throw me out."
Next day Payal handed her a note to pass around. Indu quietly put it back in Payal's bag and said, "I'm not doing this one." Two girls, Meena and Sonal, shrugged and sat down next to her.

qa.q: Who did Payal want Indu to say smelled funny?
qa.a: Payal wanted Indu to say that Rani smells funny.

qa.q: Why did Indu laugh at first even though she did not mean it?
qa.a: She was scared of being thrown out of the group, so she went along with the mean joke.

qa.q: What small step did Indu take that showed who her real friends were?
qa.a: She refused just one thing, passing the note, and saw that Meena and Sonal still sat down with her.

qa.q: What might Rani have felt when Indu apologised at the tap?
qa.a: Rani may have felt hurt but also a little relieved that Indu admitted she was wrong, though she asked why it happened.

grounding: A child goes along with mean things out of fear of being expelled, then quietly refuses one thing and sees who stands by her.
